lessons.title: The parts of a computer
lessons.html:
Getting to know the computer

Many farms and wool stores use computers for records, stock lists, wages and email. You do not need to be an expert to use one. Start by knowing the main parts.

PartWhat it does
System unit (tower) or laptop bodyThe "brain" of the computer that does the work
Monitor (screen)Shows you what the computer is doing
KeyboardUsed to type letters and numbers
Mouse or touchpadMoves the pointer on the screen and lets you click
PrinterPrints on paper
USB flash driveCarries files from one computer to another

Hardware and software

Hardware is the parts you can touch, like the keyboard and screen. Software is the programs that run on the computer, like Windows, a word processor, a spreadsheet or the farm's record program.

Important keys

  • Enter – start a new line or say "yes, do it".
  • Backspace – delete the letter to the left.
  • Delete – delete the letter to the right, or a selected item.
  • Shift – hold it to type a capital letter.
  • Space bar – makes a space between words.
  • Esc – cancel or close a box.

Using the mouse

  • Click (left button once) – choose something.
  • Double-click – open something.
  • Right-click – show a short list of options.
  • Drag – hold the left button down and move.

lessons.title: Switching on, logging in and switching off
lessons.html:
Starting and stopping the right way

Switching on

  1. Check the cables are plugged in, and the plug is switched on at the wall.
  2. Press the power button on the computer, and switch on the monitor if needed.
  3. Wait for the computer to start.

Logging in

Most computers ask for a username and password. Type them carefully. Passwords are case-sensitive: "Farm" and "farm" are different.

  • Never share your password or write it on the screen.
  • Use a password that is hard to guess, with letters and numbers.
  • Lock the computer when you walk away (on Windows, press the Windows key and L together).

The desktop

After logging in you see the desktop. It has icons (small pictures) for programs and files, the taskbar at the bottom and the Start button. Click Start to find programs.

Opening and closing programs

  • Double-click an icon, or choose it from the Start menu, to open a program.
  • Click the X in the top right corner to close it. Save your work first.

Switching off

  1. Save your work and close all programs.
  2. Click Start, then Power, then Shut down.
  3. Wait for the computer to switch off before switching off at the wall.

Never just pull out the plug. You can lose work and damage the computer. With load shedding, save your work often.

lessons.title: Looking after the computer and yourself
lessons.html:
Care and safety

Caring for the computer

  • Keep food and drinks away from the keyboard. Spills can break it.
  • Keep the computer in a clean, dry, cool place, away from dust and direct sun.
  • Do not block the air holes.
  • Use a surge protector, as power cuts and surges can damage computers.
  • Clean the screen with a soft dry cloth, with the computer switched off.
  • Do not install programs unless your supervisor or IT person allows it.

Viruses and scams

  • Do not open emails or attachments from people you do not know.
  • Do not click on strange links or pop-ups that say you won a prize.
  • Never give passwords or bank details because of an email or phone call.
  • Tell your supervisor if the computer acts strangely.

Your health

  • Sit straight with your back supported and feet flat on the floor.
  • Keep the screen at eye level, about an arm's length away.
  • Rest your eyes: look away from the screen often.
  • Stand up and stretch every hour.

Electrical safety

Do not open the computer or repair cables yourself. Report damaged plugs and cables. Never use a computer with wet hands.

Key points

  • Hardware is the parts you can touch; software is the programs.
  • Keep your password secret and lock the computer when you leave.
  • Save your work and use Shut down; never just pull the plug.
  • Keep food and drink away and do not open emails from strangers.
  • Sit straight, keep the screen at eye level and take breaks.
